title: Access change observability and SIEM backfill guidance
content:
Summary:

This note outlines a pragmatic plan to make access model changes (RBAC v2 migration and permission reshuffles) observable end-to-end, ensure audit evidence is backfilled into our SIEM, and automate evidence collection for compliance checks. It mixes design, telemetry contracts, and a staged rollout checklist focused on minimizing blind spots during the transition.

Why this matters (short):
- RBAC v2 migration will change which attributes are evaluated and which events are emitted.
- Our auditors and incident responders must see a continuous, queryable history of access changes and decision context.
- Gaps during the migration create significant risk (false positives in entitlement drift, missed escalations).

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Define a compact audit schema for access-change events and decision snapshots (pre/post state).
  - Provide a SIEM backfill plan for historical entitlement data (90-day target window).
  - Create automated evidence harvesters for rollout gates and compliance sampling.
  - Ensure low-latency routing of access-change telemetry to observability pipelines (no >5s tail for active paths).
- Non-goals:
  - Replace long-term forensic storage or change full archival retention policy (covered elsewhere).
  - Re-architect the SIEM ingestion platform. We will provide an agreed export contract.

Key definitions (how I use terms here):
- access-change: any operation that creates, updates, deletes, or scopes an entitlement, role, or policy binding.
- decision-snapshot: an encoded record capturing the input attributes and the resulting allow/deny decision for a request.
- evidence-bundle: a minimal set of artifacts (pre-state, action, post-state, actor metadata, trace id) that proves the change and its context.

Audit schema (proposal):
- event_type: access_change | decision_snapshot | delegation_event | role_rollback
- event_id: UUID v4
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- actor: {string user/principal id} (flattened as single string: "user:elena@redwood.io" or "svc:deploy-agent")
- target: resource identifier (ARN or canonical path)
- change_action: create|update|delete|bind|unbind|temporal-slice
- pre_state_summary: short descriptor (text) OR hash pointer to state blob in archival store
- post_state_summary: short descriptor (text) OR hash pointer to state blob in archival store
- reason: free text (UI or API supplied)
- decision_id: (optional) reference to decision_snapshot event_id when change triggered automated decisions
- trace_id: link to request trace / span id if change originated from an API request
- audit_tags: list of short tags (e.g., "canary-1", "sensitive:billing")

Notes on schema choices:
- Keep the top-level fields flat and textual for SIEM friendliness (avoid complex nested blobs in primary event).
- Pre/post state can be large; prefer storing full JSON blobs in object storage with a hash pointer in the event to keep SIEM ingest small and searchable.

Decision snapshot contract (what we emit on access evaluations):
- event_type: decision_snapshot
- event_id, timestamp_utc, request_id, trace_id
- principal, principal_attributes (flattened key=value; semi-colon separated)
- resource, resource_attributes (same flattened format)
- policy_version, policy_hash
- input_context_hash (points to store with full context)
- decision: allow|deny|abstain
- explanation: concise reason or top-3 rules that matched

Telemetry routing and quality-of-service:
- High-fidelity decision_snapshots for any admin-level change (create role, bind role) must be emitted synchronously and routed to the streaming pipeline (kafka-topic: access-events).
- Lower-fidelity decision snapshots for normal read-only evaluations can be sampled (1% baseline) and sent to the same pipeline with a sample_id field.
- Delivery SLA: pipeline should acknowledge within <5s; consumers (SIEM adaptor) should not add more than 20s processing tail for ingestion.

SIEM backfill plan (90-day window):
1) Scope and feasibility (week 0–1):
   - Identify canonical sources of historical entitlements: old-role-store (postgres), binding archives (s3/legacy), migration snapshots.
   - Create a mapping doc: table name -> export query -> estimated rows.
2) Export (week 1–2):
   - Export compressed NDJSON snapshots for each day in the window. Include metadata: row_created_at, row_updated_at, source_system.
3) Transform & normalize (week 2–3):
   - Apply canonicalization: normalize principal IDs, resource canonical paths, and policy version tags.
   - Compute hash pointers for each snapshot file.
4) Ingest to SIEM (week 3–4):
   - Use batched SIEM API with throttling. Keep primary event size small: one event per change_day with pointer to object store file. SIEM searchable keys: principal, resource, change_action, timestamp.
5) Validation & reconciliation (week 4–5):
   - Random sample checks: pick 500 change events and verify object store blob + SIEM event parity.
   - Run queries used by audits and incident response to verify expected time series.

Evidence automation (rollout gates and sampling):
- Gate 0: pre-cutover smoke. Automated script creates a snapshot of current role bindings and posts to compliance channel.
- Gate 1: canary (5% of tenants). For every canary change: emit decision_snapshot (full) + access_change evidence-bundle to object store. Run nightly comparator job.
- Gate 2: broad rollout. Enable 10% sampling of decision_snapshots and enrich with pre/post blobs for any admin action.
- Gate 3: complete. Emit full decision_snapshots for admin events and 1% sampling of all evaluations.

Sampling & retention policy recommendations:
- Full admin-level events: retain full blobs for 365 days in warm storage.
- Sampled evaluations: retain index events in SIEM for 90 days, full blobs for 30 days.
- Hash pointers to blobs should be immutable and include a checksum to assist forensic verification.

Operational runbook (short):
- To re-run backfill for a date range: run scripts/backfill/export_range.sh --from YYYY-MM-DD --to YYYY-MM-DD. It will produce ndjson in s3://redwood-audit-backfill/YYYY/MM/DD/
- To validate SIEM ingestion: tools/siem-validate.py --sample 200 --since YYYY-MM-DD. Outputs CSV with mismatches.
- To generate evidence bundle for a specific event_id: tools/make_evidence_bundle --event-id <uuid> -> writes ZIP to s3://redwood-audit-bundles/<event_id>.zip

Metrics to watch during migration:
- ingestion_success_rate (per-minute) for access-events topic >= 99.5%
- decision_snapshot_tail: 95th percentile latency <= 5s for admin events
- SIEM_ingest_throughput: events/sec and bytes/sec (watch for spikes)
- mismatch_rate between source-of-truth and SIEM after backfill <= 0.1%

Rollout checklist (practical):
- [ ] Confirm export queries for all entitlement stores (owner: DataEng)
- [ ] Prepare object storage with lifecycle (owner: Infra)
- [ ] Implement lightweight event schema in API layer (owner: AuthService)
- [ ] Implement synchronous emit for admin flows (owner: AuthService)
- [ ] Wire Kafka topic and ensure retention policy (owner: Observability)
- [ ] Implement SIEM adaptor with rate limiting and idempotency (owner: Observability)
- [ ] Run dry-run backfill for past 7 days and validate (owner: Security)
- [ ] Schedule canary with customer-ops and product (owner: Product)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much of the pre/post state do we store inline vs external object store? Recommendation: keep top-level SIEM events small and reference object store for full JSON.
- Sampling strategy for high-cardinality evaluation paths (embedding service, inference logs). Recommendation: focus sampling on admin/tenant-scoped changes and aggressive deduplication of user-level evaluations.
- Compliance ask: some auditors want inline evidence for 180 days. This conflicts with SIEM size limits. Option: provide a secondary archival export (on-demand) for audit windows.

Appendix: example NDJSON event (flattened for SIEM)
{
  "event_type": "access_change",
  "event_id": "4f5a1b2e-...",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-02-12T18:22:13Z",
  "actor": "user:maya@redwood.io",
  "target": "project:billing/service-account:read-only",
  "change_action": "bind",
  "pre_state_summary": "role-binding: none",
  "post_state_summary": "role-binding: role-read-only-v2",
  "audit_tags": "canary-3;sensitive:billing",
  "object_blob_hash": "sha256:abc123...",
  "trace_id": "span-84a2"
}

Next steps (this week):
- Align on schema changes with Observability and AuthService (meeting scheduled Thu).
- Hand off export queries to DataEng for cost/row estimates.
- Create minimal proof-of-concept that emits decision_snapshot for a single admin flow and lands in kafka.

Notes to reviewers: please pay attention to the retention ladder and the proposed sampling percentages. If auditors insist on inline full JSON in SIEM for >90 days we should cost out index growth and consider a dedicated archival SIEM project.
